meta.title: OctoLoop | Multi-agent workflow built on Octos
meta.description: OctoLoop pairs an inner execution agent with an outer review agent. See how the OLP protocol, peer workers, and evidence-driven improvement loop fit together.

home.label: Reference application · multi-agent
home.heading: OctoLoop: execution inside, review outside
home.description: OctoLoop uses Octoscode and Octos for the inner execution loop, and an independent CLI agent for planning and review. The Outer-Loop Protocol (OLP) defines how they exchange work and evidence.

inner.name: Inner agent
inner.description: An Octos master agent works on the goal, delegates bounded tasks to peers, tests changes, commits, and records what happened.

outer.name: Outer agent
outer.description: A separate CLI agent reads the review board and event trail, checks the diff in an isolated worktree, and decides what needs another pass.

home.handoff: A review board, delivery records, goal ledger, and Git commits carry the handoff between the two loops.
home.evolution: Review ACKs, runtime events, and MCP audit records can be collected into symptom cards. A retrospective groups recurring failures; the outer agent turns approved findings into protocol, tooling, or contract-test changes.
home.evolutionStatus: Collection and retrospective run manually by default.

page.label: Multi-agent reference application
page.heading: OctoLoop
page.lead: A two-loop coding workflow built from Octos execution, Octoscode TUI, an independent outer agent, and a written review protocol. It separates implementation from acceptance without tying either role to one model vendor.
page.flowDescription: The operator sets the goal. The inner loop executes and reports; the outer loop verifies and feeds concrete corrections back. Under OLP, accepted commits are pushed by the outer loop.

flow.name: 01 · Assign
flow.description: The operator sets the goal and permissions. The outer agent records scoped guidance on the review board.

flow.name: 02 · Execute
flow.description: The inner master advances the goal, can hand off tasks to peers, runs checks, commits, and writes an ACK with its verification status.

flow.name: 03 · Review
flow.description: The outer agent reads the ledger, delivery record, and diff, then independently reruns relevant checks in an isolated worktree.

flow.name: 04 · Decide
flow.description: The outer agent accepts or returns a numbered correction. Permission changes and other operator decisions go back to the human.

page.innerOutput: Output: commit, result record, and ACK(done | wontdo | blocked).
page.outerOutput: Output: accepted review or a numbered correction. Under OLP, the inner loop does not push; the outer loop handles push after acceptance.
boundaries: The review board carries numbered, dated guidance. The inner agent acknowledges each active item; acknowledged history is not replayed.
Peer agents can work in separate sessions and Git worktrees. A result record, goal ledger, and Git diff make the handoff inspectable.
A delivery states what was verified. The outer agent checks the claim independently and can request another pass.
An inner agent may report a blocker or ask the outer agent through the optional OLP MCP channel. Approval and scope changes remain operator decisions.
page.evolutionLead: OctoLoop's evolution loop turns observed friction into reviewed changes to the workflow. The current collection and retrospective commands are manual by default.

evolution.name: Collect evidence
evolution.description: The harvest script reads active-board ACKs, runtime events, and the MCP audit board. It deduplicates signals into symptom cards in .octos/EVOLUTION.md.

evolution.name: Group recurring failures
evolution.description: The retrospective groups cards by normalized symptoms and produces candidate briefs and FLAW record drafts.

evolution.name: Review the change
evolution.description: The outer reviewer validates the cause, files an accepted FLAW record, and turns it into a protocol, tool, or contract-test change that can be verified.

page.evolutionTools: Tools: olp-evo-harvest.sh and olp-evo-retro.sh. After a FLAW record is accepted, olp-evo-spec-skeleton.sh can generate a contract-test skeleton.
page.evolutionNote: The scripts produce evidence and drafts. A reviewer still decides what becomes a tracked change; collection alone does not modify the running agents.
startSteps: Install Octoscode TUI and complete its first-run profile and provider setup.
Use the OctoLoop quickstart and olp-init.sh from the Octoscode repository to set up the project review board and inner-loop instructions.
Run the inner loop in the project, then connect a separate outer CLI agent using the OLP role and review rules. Add model lanes or peer workers as the work requires.
When review evidence accumulates, run the harvest and retrospective scripts, inspect the candidate records, and make approved changes through the normal review cycle.
